thread:
maria: quick sync  follow up to the handshake RFC. idea: emit a tiny PRIMED event at ingest to reserve an estimated token hold so late attribution doesn't create spikes or double-billing. outline + tradeoffs below.

jonathan: please paste the minimal event shape and RFC link.

maria: RFC: https://go/repo/rfcs/handshake-priming. minimal priming event:
```json
{
  "type": "primed",
  "priming_id": "uuid-prim-9a8b",
  "acct": "tenant-123",
  "est_tokens": 42,
  "ingest_ts": 1755556789
}
```
Super small, no heavy provenance. Just enough to decrement a soft pool and create a compact audit pointer.

kevin: main tradeoff: fidelity vs SLO. keeping raw events until finalize makes audits simple but costs a lot. priming helps latency but opens a mismatch window. how long keep the primed delta?

alice: proposal: keep compact proof-frames for 90d, and retain a fingerprint index for 1y for long-tail audits. proof-frame = tiny fingerprint + pointers, no payload. rehydrate when needed.

kevin: if priming underestimates, do we bill final or stick with primed? refunds are messy.

maria: options: (A) conservative priming (+X% buffer), (B) reconcile small deltas weekly, (C) put primed amount into a billing "hold" and charge final amount at finalize so customers don't see double charges. leaning to C.

jonathan: C is better UX but needs clear state machine: PRIMED -> FINALIZED -> COMMITTED/RECONCILED. idempotency is critical.

alice: ingest should include priming_id + watermark. final events with same priming_id trigger reconciliation and emit an audit_replay record. reduces duplicate risk.

kevin: for p99, keep priming fast-path in memory (fast KV) and async flush to object store. avoid blocking calls on durable writes.

maria: agreed. critical-path writes -> in-memory ledger with background durable checkpointing. gives p99 while preserving eventual auditability.

sre-bot: metric update - priming-write ingest-lag p50=15ms p95=80ms p99=300ms (last 5m).

kevin: p99 seems high. make priming write best-effort (no fsync) and add deferred-queue for failures so we never block API calls.

alice: compaction notes: proof-frames TTL 90d, fingerprint index 1y. compaction pipeline drops payloads but keeps fingerprint->object pointer mapping.

maria: consensus so far:
- emit PRIMED event in ingest fast-path (tiny)
- maintain proof-frames 90d, fingerprint index 1y
- state machine PRIMED->FINALIZED->COMMITTED with priming_id for idempotency
- deferred-queue for priming failures + conservative overestimate (+10%)

jonathan: i'll prototype the in-memory ledger shim + priming_id API this week.

kevin: add audit header x-accounting-proof: <fingerprint> to routed events and emit a small link event mapping priming->final for forensic joins.

alice: i'll run TCO estimates for S3 + index retention and post numbers by Friday. will also add compaction load tests.

maria: owners: jonathan (proto), alice (cost model & compaction), kevin (SLA/failure modes). i'll file a short follow-up RFC with state transitions and sample events.

jonathan: question  reconciliation window? 24h or 7d?

maria: default 7d for auto-reconcile, tenant-configurable down to 24h.

kevin: fallback: if finalize never arrives after window, move primed hold -> release and mark audit as stale_priming. audits must show that path.

alice: add resolved_via: [final|timeout|manual] on finalization events so billing can filter.

maria: good. i'll include that.

jonathan: i'll push WIP branch and share link.

kevin: one more ask  add a compact-mode test harness simulating 10k delayed final events to validate compaction/rehydration throughput.

alice: noted will add load tests.

maria: thanks all :thumbsup: will create the RFC and invite reviews. closing thread.
